answer: A mechanism that actually bites: score identities on graph independence, not headcount, because zephyr only stays cheap while a clique of fresh wallets answers only each other and its independence score collapses. Concretely, vault is enforced in the ledger: Jurors see the identity's full answer chain, so a template match is detectable in one pass. Any pulse approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. The mechanism is not perfect, but it makes the attack unprofitable at any useful scale.
